config.title: TanStack Query Basics

intro.title: TanStack Query Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that fetches and displays a list of posts from a mock API. You'll learn the core concept of server-state management using TanStack Query (also known as @tanstack/angular-query) to handle data fetching, caching, and synchronization. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and the TanStack Query library with its hooks like useQuery. By the end, you'll understand how to efficiently load and manage remote data in your Angular apps with less boilerplate code.
intro.usecase: In real applications, TanStack Query (Angular Query) powers dynamic data displays where fresh information is critical. You'll see it in dashboard widgets showing live metrics, e-commerce product listings with real-time inventory updates, and admin panels displaying user activity logs. This pattern handles the complex logic of fetching, caching, and synchronizing server state behind common UI components like data tables, search filters, and auto-refreshing charts. As a developer, you'll use it to build responsive interfaces that feel instant to users while efficiently managing network requests and error states.

objectives: Initialize TanStack Query in an Angular application by installing dependencies and configuring the QueryClient
Implement a query hook to fetch data from a REST API endpoint
Configure query options to control caching, retries, and stale time behavior
Integrate query results into Angular components by binding data to templates
Manipulate UI states by conditionally rendering loading, error, and success interfaces
Construct a mutation hook to update server data and invalidate related queries
Apply query invalidation patterns to refresh data after mutations complete

steps.title: Import required Angular and TanStack Query modules
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core', HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http', and the necessary TanStack Query modules: provideQueryClient, QueryClient, QueryClientProvider from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your TypeScript file. Each import should be on its own line or combined with commas.
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular and TanStack Query modules are imported, enabling you to use Angular components, HTTP client, and TanStack Query features.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core', HttpClientModule is imported from '@angular/common/http', and provideQueryClient, QueryClient, QueryClientProvider are imported from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but not all required ones. Check that you have Component, HttpClientModule, and the three TanStack Query modules: provideQueryClient, QueryClient, and QueryClientProvider.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Ensure you import Component from '@angular/core', HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http', and provideQueryClient, QueryClient, QueryClientProvider from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'.

steps.title: Create and configure the QueryClient
steps.instruction: Create a QueryClient instance with default options inside your component or service.
steps.hint: Instantiate a new QueryClient and assign it to a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a service instance
const httpClient = new HttpClient();
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required modules here

// Create a QueryClient instance here
steps.expectedOutcome: A QueryClient instance is created and ready to be used for data fetching.
successCriteria: A QueryClient instance is created with default options.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a QueryClient instance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're creating a QueryClient instance with the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Try creating a QueryClient instance with default options.

steps.title: Create a data service with HttpClient
steps.instruction: Create an Angular service named 'DataService' that injects HttpClient and defines a method to fetch data from a public API endpoint.
steps.hint: Generate the service using Angular CLI conventions: create a class with @Injectable decorator, inject HttpClient in the constructor, and add a method that returns an observable.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DataService class is created with HttpClient injected and a method defined for making API calls.
successCriteria: DataService class exists with @Injectable decorator, HttpClient injected in constructor, and at least one method that returns an Observable from HttpClient.get.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your service has: 1) @Injectable decorator with providedIn: 'root', 2) HttpClient injected in constructor, 3) a method that returns this.http.get() with a URL.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service isn't properly set up. Remember to: create a class with @Injectable, inject HttpClient in constructor, and define a method that returns an HTTP GET request.

steps.title: Define the main component structure
steps.instruction: Create the main Angular component class named 'QueryDemoComponent' with the @Component decorator and basic structure.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' and define a class with a selector, template, and styles.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main Angular component class is created with proper decorator and structure, ready to use TanStack Query.
successCriteria: Component class 'QueryDemoComponent' is defined with @Component decorator containing selector, template, and styles properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure to include all required parts: the @Component decorator with selector, template, and styles properties, and export the class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a class named 'QueryDemoComponent' with the @Component decorator containing selector, template, and styles properties.

steps.title: Inject the data service into the component
steps.instruction: In the QueryDemoComponent class, add a constructor that injects the DataService as a dependency.
steps.hint: Use the constructor parameter with the appropriate type annotation to inject the service.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: injecting a service into a component
constructor(private dataService: DataService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has access to the DataService instance through dependency injection.
successCriteria: The QueryDemoComponent constructor includes a parameter of type DataService with appropriate access modifier.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the constructor parameter has the correct type annotation and access modifier.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor should inject the DataService. Check that you've added a parameter with the proper type and access modifier.

steps.title: Set up the useQuery hook in the component
steps.instruction: Inside the QueryDemoComponent class, add a property called 'postsQuery' that uses the useQuery hook to fetch data from the DataService's getPosts method.
steps.hint: Use the useQuery hook from @tanstack/angular-query-experimental. The query key should be ['posts'] and the query function should call this.dataService.getPosts().
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a postsQuery property that configures TanStack Query to fetch posts data.
successCriteria: The QueryDemoComponent has a postsQuery property that uses useQuery with queryKey ['posts'] and queryFn calling this.dataService.getPosts()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct queryKey and calling the dataService method properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useQuery setup isn't quite right. Check that you're using the correct syntax and calling the dataService method.

steps.title: Configure the query key and query function
steps.instruction: Inside the QueryDemoComponent class, configure the postsQuery property by calling useQuery with a query key array and a query function that calls this.dataService.getPosts().
steps.hint: The useQuery hook takes an object with queryKey and queryFn properties. For queryKey, use an array like ['posts']. For queryFn, call this.dataService.getPosts() and convert the Observable to a Promise with .toPromise().
steps.expectedOutcome: The postsQuery property will be properly configured with a query key and query function that fetches posts from the data service.
successCriteria: The postsQuery property is defined with useQuery, containing a queryKey array with 'posts' and a queryFn that calls this.dataService.getPosts().toPromise().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling useQuery with both queryKey and queryFn properties. The queryFn should convert the Observable to a Promise.
steps.feedbackWrong: The query configuration isn't complete. Remember to use useQuery with an object containing queryKey and queryFn properties.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template to your QueryDemoComponent class with a basic container div that will display the fetched posts data.
steps.hint: In Angular components, you can add a template using the @Component decorator's template property. Start with a simple div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The QueryDemoComponent now has a template property with a container div element, ready for displaying data.
successCriteria: The component's template property contains a div element as the main container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element inside the template property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain a div element. Check that you've properly added it to the template property in the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Display loading state in the template
steps.instruction: In the QueryDemoComponent template, add a paragraph element that shows a loading message when the postsQuery is in loading state. Use the postsQuery.isLoading property to conditionally render this paragraph.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax with *ngIf to conditionally show the loading message based on postsQuery.isLoading.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional loading display in Angular template

Loading data...
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a paragraph that displays a loading message when the query is fetching data.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element with *ngIf="postsQuery.isLoading" that shows a loading message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct property (postsQuery.isLoading) and Angular's *ngIf directive to conditionally show the loading message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show a loading message when the query is loading. Remember to use postsQuery.isLoading with *ngIf to conditionally render a paragraph with loading text.

steps.title: Add a refresh button to refetch data
steps.instruction: Add a button to the template that calls the refetch method from the postsQuery result when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding and call postsQuery.refetch() in the handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the template that, when clicked, triggers a manual refetch of the posts data using TanStack Query's refetch method.
successCriteria: The template contains a button with (click) event binding that calls postsQuery.refetch().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it might not be properly wired to the refetch method. Make sure you're calling postsQuery.refetch() in the click handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The refresh button is missing or not properly configured. Add a button that calls the refetch method when clicked.
